No, SVG conversion isn't needed. The `extract_otp_secrets` tool works directly with JPG/PNG images - it uses a QR code reader library (pyzbar) to decode them.

The potential challenge with these photos is **image quality**, not format:
- Some are at an angle
- There are reflections on the screen
- Some appear slightly blurry

If the tool has trouble reading them, options would be:
1. Crop the images to just the QR code area
2. Take new screenshots directly from the phone (cleaner than photos of a screen)
3. Use the "Export accounts" feature in Google Authenticator to get the `otpauth-migration://` URI text directly

Want me to try running `extract_otp_secrets` on these images as-is to see if it can decode them?

ASSISTANT (line 70):
----------------------------------------
The QR codes can't be decoded from these photos. The issues are:

1. **Photos of a screen** - reflections and moiré patterns interfere
2. **Angled shots** - perspective distortion
3. **Screen glare/blur** - reduces contrast

**Solutions:**

1. **Take screenshots directly on the phone** instead of photos of the screen, then transfer them

2. **If you still have access to Google Authenticator**, go to the export screen again and take a direct screenshot (power + volume down on most phones)

3. **Alternative approach**: Some phones let you share/copy the migration URI text. If you can get the `otpauth-migration://offline?data=...` text string, paste it here and I can decode it directly.

Would you like to try one of these approaches?

ASSISTANT (line 342):
----------------------------------------
The issue with your current URL is the **hardcoded date** (`2025-12`). For automatic updates, use a URL that always fetches the latest version.

**For DB-IP free database**, use this pattern:
```
https://download.db-ip.com/free/dbip-city-lite-YYYY-MM.mmdb.gz
```

Unfortunately, DB-IP doesn't provide a "latest" symlink for free databases. **Options:**

### Option 1: Use MaxMind GeoLite2 (Recommended for auto-updates)
1. Create free account at https://www.maxmind.com/en/geolite2/signup
2. Go to Account → Manage License Keys → Generate new license key
3. Your download URL will be:
```
https://download.maxmind.com/app/geoip_download?edition_id=GeoLite2-City&license_key=YOUR_LICENSE_KEY&suffix=tar.gz
```

### Option 2: Keep DB-IP but update monthly
The free DB-IP URL changes monthly. You'd need to manually update it or set up a cron job to download and update it.

### Option 3: Use Matomo's built-in updater
In Matomo:
1. Go to **Administration → System → Geolocation**
2. Select **"DBIP / GeoIP 2 (Php)"**
3. If you use MaxMind with a license key, paste the URL with your key

**Which database provider do you want to use?** MaxMind GeoLite2 is free and supports proper automatic updates with a license key.

● Web Search("Brave browser password manager JSON import export sync 2025")
  ⎿  Did 1 search in 8s                                                                                                                      

● Short answer: You'll need a dedicated password manager for JSON files with category organization.

  Here's the breakdown:

  Brave's Built-in Password Manager

  - Export/Import format: CSV only (not JSON)
  - Syncing: Works via Brave Sync (decentralized, end-to-end encrypted across Brave devices)
  - Organization: Basic - passwords are saved but not organized by custom categories
  - Security note: CSV exports are unencrypted, so you need to store them securely

  What You Want (JSON with Categories)

  Brave's built-in doesn't support this. You'd need a dedicated password manager like:

  1. Bitwarden - Open-source, supports JSON import/export, has category/folder organization, syncs across devices
  2. 1Password - Can import from Brave, supports organized vaults
  3. Proton Pass - Privacy-focused, supports password organization
  4. KeePass - Local-only, uses encrypted database files, fully customizable with categories

  Recommendation

  If you want:
  - JSON file format with category organization
  - Easy sync across devices
  - Strong privacy

  Go with Bitwarden - it's free, open-source, has browser extensions, supports JSON, and you can self-host it. You can also organize passwords
   in custom folders/categories.

  Brave's built-in is fine for basic password storage synced across Brave devices, but it's not flexible enough for your JSON + category
  requirements.

  Sources:
  - https://support.brave.app/hc/en-us/articles/360019782291-How-do-I-import-or-export-browsing-data
  - https://ihaveapc.com/2025/09/how-to-export-and-import-passwords-in-brave-browser/

The "push to approve" feature depends on **both the app AND the service supporting it**. Here's the breakdown:

**Apps with push approval:**

| App | Push Approval | Notes |
|-----|--------------|-------|
| **Microsoft Authenticator** | Yes | For Microsoft accounts only |
| **Google Authenticator** | Yes | For Google accounts only (Google Prompt) |
| **Duo Mobile** | Yes | For services that integrate Duo |
| **Authy** | Limited | OneTouch for Twilio-integrated services |
| **1Password** | No | TOTP only |
| **Bitwarden** | No | TOTP only |
| **Aegis** | No | TOTP only |

**The catch:** Push approval requires the **service** (GitHub, Google, etc.) to support that specific app's push protocol. It's not universal.

**GitHub specifically:**
- Push approval **only works with GitHub Mobile app** - no third-party authenticator supports it

**Best universal solution: Passkeys**
- One tap/biometric to approve
- No codes to type
- Works with: GitHub, Google, Microsoft, many others
- Stored in: phone biometrics, hardware key (YubiKey), or password manager

**My recommendation:**
- Use **Aegis** for TOTP codes (the 30 accounts we extracted)
- Enable **Passkeys** where available (GitHub, Google, etc.) for tap-to-approve experience

    │               └─► YubiKey tap
    │
    └─► Passkey (replaces password + 2FA)

            └─► Biometric or YubiKey tap
```

## Complete Security Stack: Web + Terminal

| Layer | Web (Browser) | Terminal (CLI) |
|-------|---------------|----------------|
| **Passwords** | Bitwarden extension | `bw` CLI / `pass` |

| **GPG Keys** | N/A | `~/.gnupg/` or YubiKey |
| **Hardware** | YubiKey tap | YubiKey tap |

## Authentication Flows

```
WEB LOGIN                          TERMINAL/SSH
    │                                   │
    ├─► Password (Bitwarden)            ├─► SSH Key (~/.ssh/id_ed25519)
    │       │                           │       │
    │       └─► 2FA                     │       └─► Key passphrase
    │           ├─► TOTP (Aegis)        │           └─► OR YubiKey tap
    │           ├─► YubiKey tap         │
    │           └─► Passkey             ├─► GPG signing (git commits)
    │                                   │       └─► YubiKey tap
    └─► Passkey only (no password)      │
            └─► YubiKey tap             └─► sudo / sensitive ops
                                                └─► YubiKey PAM
```

## YubiKey Slots for Terminal

| Slot | Use |
|------|-----|
| **FIDO2** | Passkeys, SSH (ed25519-sk) |
| **PIV** | SSH, certificates, smartcard |
| **OpenPGP** | GPG keys, git signing |
| **OTP** | Legacy TOTP backup |

## SSH Options with YubiKey

```bash
# Option 1: FIDO2 SSH key (modern, recommended)
ssh-keygen -t ed25519-sk -C "yubikey"

# Option 2: GPG-based SSH via YubiKey
gpg --card-status
export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$(gpgconf --list-dirs agent-ssh-socket)

# Option 3: PIV-based SSH
yubico-piv-tool -a generate -s 9a
```

## Use Cases

| Data | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| **Addresses** | Shipping, billing, KYC verification |
| **Phones** | SMS 2FA codes, account recovery, verification calls |
| **Payment Cards** | Purchases, ID verification (small charge/refund), subscriptions |
| **Personal IDs** | KYC for crypto, banking, etc. |

## Integration with Bitwarden

Bitwarden has built-in types for this:
- **Identity** → Addresses, names
- **Card** → Payment cards
- **Secure Note** → Phones linked to services, IDs

The `identity_template.json` file is ready for you to fill in with your data, then you can import the important parts into Bitwarden.

USER (line 766):
========================================
bitwarden.eu vs selfhosted?

----------------------------------------
ASSISTANT (line 768):
----------------------------------------
**Comparison:**

| Aspect | bitwarden.eu (Cloud) | Self-hosted (Vaultwarden) |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------------|
| **Setup** | Instant, no maintenance | Need server, updates, backups |
| **Cost** | Free / $10/yr premium | Free (your server costs) |
| **TOTP** | Premium only ($10/yr) | Free (all features unlocked) |
| **Data location** | EU (GDPR compliant) | Your server |
| **Uptime** | 99.9% SLA | You manage it |
| **Security updates** | Automatic | Manual (or watchtower) |
| **Passkey sync** | Yes | Yes |
| **Emergency access** | Yes | Yes |

**My recommendation given your setup:**

You already have Oracle VMs. Running **Vaultwarden** (lightweight Rust implementation) is trivial:

```bash
docker run -d --name vaultwarden \
  -v /vw-data/:/data/ \
  -p 8080:80 \
  vaultwarden/server:latest
```

**However**, for a password manager specifically:
- **bitwarden.eu** = less attack surface, no self-maintenance
- **Self-hosted** = full control, but you're responsible for security

Since you're using Aegis for TOTP anyway (not Bitwarden's TOTP), the $10/yr premium isn't needed. **bitwarden.eu free tier** might be the sweet spot - zero maintenance, EU data residency, and you keep TOTP in Aegis.

What's your priority - full control or zero maintenance?

USER (line 770):
========================================
but what about being able to export and import files is possible using the bitwarden to do it torugh api?

----------------------------------------
ASSISTANT (line 772):
----------------------------------------
Yes, Bitwarden has a CLI and API for import/export:

**Bitwarden CLI** (works with both cloud and self-hosted):
```bash
# Install
npm install -g @bitwarden/cli

# Login
bw login

# Export (JSON or CSV)
bw export --format json --output vault_backup.json

# Import
bw import bitwarden_json vault_backup.json
```

**API Access:**

| Feature | bitwarden.eu | Self-hosted |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| CLI export/import | Yes | Yes |
| Public API | Organizations only (paid) | Yes (full) |
| Vault API | Via CLI only | Direct access |
| Automated backups | CLI + cron | CLI + cron OR direct DB |

**For your use case (LOCAL_KEYS sync):**

```bash
# Export to your LOCAL_KEYS folder
bw sync
bw export --format json > /home/diego/Documents/Git/LOCAL_KEYS/02_browser/bitwarden_vault.json

# Import from your consolidated files
bw import bitwarden_json passwords.json
```

**Self-hosted advantage:** Direct database access for backups
```bash
# Vaultwarden - just backup the SQLite
cp /vw-data/db.sqlite3 /backup/
```

**Cloud advantage:** Zero maintenance, CLI works the same

Both options support full programmatic access via CLI. The main difference is self-hosted gives you direct database access for simpler backups.

USER (line 774):
========================================
can i start with bitwarden.eu and in the future migrate to self-hosted?

----------------------------------------
ASSISTANT (line 776):
----------------------------------------
Yes, migration is simple:

```bash
# 1. Export from bitwarden.eu
bw config server https://vault.bitwarden.eu
bw login
bw export --format json > vault_backup.json

# 2. Setup Vaultwarden on your server
docker run -d --name vaultwarden -v /vw-data/:/data/ -p 8080:80 vaultwarden/server

# 3. Import to self-hosted
bw config server https://vault.yourdomain.com
bw login
bw import bitwarden_json vault_backup.json
```

**What migrates:**
- All passwords
- Identities
- Cards
- Secure notes
- Folder structure
- TOTP secrets (if any)

**What doesn't migrate:**
- Attachments (re-upload manually)
- Send links (recreate)
- Organization data (separate export)

**Recommendation:** Start with bitwarden.eu. If you later want self-hosted, it's a 5-minute migration. No lock-in.

USER (line 802):
========================================
what is PIN fallback?

----------------------------------------
ASSISTANT (line 804):
----------------------------------------
**PIN fallback** = If fingerprint fails, use a PIN code instead.

```
YubiKey Bio Authentication
==========================

Attempt 1: Fingerprint ──► ❌ Failed (wet finger?)
Attempt 2: Fingerprint ──► ❌ Failed
Attempt 3: Fingerprint ──► ❌ Failed
           │
           ▼
      ┌─────────────┐
      │ Enter PIN:  │
      │ ****        │  ◄── Fallback option
      └─────────────┘
```

**Why it exists:**
- Wet/dirty fingers
- Injury to finger
- Cold weather (poor reading)
- Fingerprint sensor damaged

**Security:**

| Scenario | Access |
|----------|--------|
| Fingerprint works | Instant unlock |
| Fingerprint fails 3x | PIN required |
| PIN wrong 8x | YubiKey **locks permanently** |

**You set the PIN** when you first configure the YubiKey. It's a backup, not a weakness - the 8-attempt limit prevents brute force.

So: Fingerprint = convenient, PIN = fallback, both = your security.

USER (line 810):
========================================
if the yubikey is a pendrive how would i input the pin?

----------------------------------------
ASSISTANT (line 812):
----------------------------------------
The PIN is entered on **your computer/phone screen**, not on the YubiKey itself.

```
Authentication Flow
===================

1. Plug in YubiKey
        │
        ▼
2. Browser/OS shows prompt:
   ┌─────────────────────────┐
   │  Enter YubiKey PIN:     │
   │  ┌───────────────────┐  │
   │  │ ****              │  │  ◄── Type on keyboard
   │  └───────────────────┘  │
   │         [OK]            │
   └─────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼
3. Computer sends PIN to YubiKey
        │
        ▼
4. YubiKey verifies internally
        │
        ▼
5. ✅ Touch YubiKey to confirm (or fingerprint on Bio)
```

**YubiKey Bio flow:**
```
Option A: Touch fingerprint sensor ──► Instant (no PIN needed)
Option B: Fingerprint fails 3x ──► Browser asks for PIN ──► Type on keyboard
```

The YubiKey stores and validates the PIN internally - your computer just sends it over USB. The PIN never leaves the YubiKey's secure chip.

Default choice.\n   119→* **Vue 3:** Used for complex Type 3 applications requiring state management (MyFeed).\n   120→* **SvelteKit:** Used for Type 2/4 Hybrid applications needing SEO + interactivity (MyGames, MyProfile).\n   121→* **React+Vite:** Used for Type 2/3 SPAs requiring client-side rendering with modern tooling (MyMaps).\n   122→* **Next.js:** React-based framework for Type 4 applications with SSR/SSG capabilities.\n   123→\n   124→### CSS Strategy\n   125→* **Sass:** The default styling engine for custom designs. JS is only for sprinkles (menus, dark mode).\n   131→* **Client-Side (CSR):** The server sends an empty HTML shell. JS populates the DOM.\n   132→* **Hybrid (Hydrated):** The server sends populated HTML (for SEO), then JS "wakes up" the page.\n   133→\n   134→\n   135→### Build -> Render DOM -> Render DOM+CSS\n   136→\n   137→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n   138→  │                         WHO DOES THE WORK?                                   │\n   139→  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n   140→  │                                                                              │\n   141→  │   BUILD TIME              SERVER TIME              CLIENT TIME               │\n   142→  │   (Developer\'s PC)        (Server per request)     (User\'s Browser)          │\n   143→  │                                                                              │\n   144→  │   ┌─────────────┐         ┌─────────────┐         ┌─────────────┐           │\n   145→  │   │ Compile     │         │ Generate    │         │ Parse HTML  │           │\n   146→  │   │ Bundle      │         │ HTML        │         │ Execute JS  │           │\n   147→  │   │ Minify      │         │ Fetch data  │         │ Paint CSS   │           │\n   148→  │   │ Optimize    │         │ Render      │         │ Layout      │           │\n   149→  │   └─────────────┘         └─────────────┘         └─────────────┘           │\n   150→  │                                                                              │\n   151→  │   Cost: Once              Cost: Per request        Cost: Per user            │\n   152→  │   Paid by: You            Paid by: Server          Paid by: User\'s device    │\n   153→  │                                                                              │\n   154→  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n   155→\n   156→  Three Types of Work\n   157→\n   158→  1. | File | Change |
|------|--------|

**3. How It Works:**

```
cloud_dash.py --export js
       ↓
local-data.js (LOCAL_DATA = {...})
       ↓

       ↓
main.ts (Local button toggles mode)
       ↓
Dashboard uses local or API data
```

## Current `cloud_dash.py` Capabilities

### ✅ Already Implemented

| Feature | TUI | API | Method |
|---------|-----|-----|--------|
| **View VM Status** | ✅ | ✅ | SSH ping check |
| **View RAM/Disk** | ✅ | ✅ | `free -m`, `df -h` |
| **View Containers** | ✅ | ✅ | `docker ps` |
| **Reboot VM** | ✅ `[3]` | ✅ `/api/vm/{id}/reboot` | `sudo reboot` |
| **Restart Container** | ✅ `[4]` | ❌ | `docker restart` |
| **Stop/Start Container** | ✅ `[6]` | ❌ | `docker stop/start` |
| **View Logs** | ✅ `[5]` | ❌ | `docker logs` |
| **Start OCI Instance** | ❌ | ✅ | `oci compute instance action --action START` |
| **Export (json/csv/html/js)** | ✅ | ❌ | File export |

### ❌ Missing for Full Control

| Feature | Difficulty | Implementation |
|---------|------------|----------------|
| **Deploy Service** | Medium | `docker-compose up -d` |
| **Scale Containers** | Medium | `docker-compose scale` |
| **Update Container** | Medium | `docker pull && restart` |
| **Create/Delete VM** | Hard | OCI/GCloud CLI |
| **Backup Database** | Medium | `docker exec` + dump |
| **View Container Logs (API)** | Easy | Add endpoint |
| **Stop/Start Container (API)** | Easy | Add endpoint |
| **SSH Terminal (Web)** | Hard | WebSocket + xterm.js |

### Current TUI Menu
```
[1] VM Details    [2] Containers   [3] Reboot VM    
[4] Restart Container    [5] Logs    [6] Stop/Start
```

1. Deploy/Update container endpoints

## Full Infrastructure Management Implementation Complete

I've implemented the complete cloud infrastructure management system with OAuth2 control. Here's what was added:

### Backend (cloud_dash.py)
**New API Endpoints** (all require GitHub OAuth2):
- `POST /api/vm/{vm_id}/container/{container}/stop` - Stop container
- `POST /api/vm/{vm_id}/container/{container}/start` - Start container  
- `POST /api/vm/{vm_id}/container/{container}/restart` - Restart container
- `GET /api/vm/{vm_id}/container/{container}/logs?lines=100` - Get logs
- `POST /api/vm/{vm_id}/container/{container}/update` - Pull new image & restart
- `POST /api/service/{service_id}/deploy` - Deploy with docker-compose
- `POST /api/vm/{vm_id}/backup` - Backup databases (auto-detects MySQL/PostgreSQL)
- `POST /api/auth/github/callback` - JSON OAuth callback endpoint

### Frontend
**New Files Created:**
- `typescript/admin-actions.ts` - OAuth2 auth + API calls for all admin actions
- `scss/components/_admin.scss` - Admin button styles (logs, stop, start, restart, update, backup, deploy)
- `oauth-callback.html` - OAuth2 callback page

**Updated Files:**
- `main.ts` - Added auth button + container admin buttons initialization
- `index.html` - Added Admin section with auth container
- `scss/main.scss` - Included admin styles

### How It Works
1. **Local Mode**: Open `dist_vanilla/index.html` directly - uses `local-data.js` (generated via `python cloud_dash.py --export js`)
2. **API Mode**: Toggle to "API" for live data from Flask backend
3. **Admin Actions**: Click "Login" to authenticate with GitHub, then admin buttons become active
4. **OAuth2 Security**: Only users in `GITHUB_ALLOWED_USERS` (diegonmarcos) can execute admin actions

### Files in dist_vanilla/
```
index.html       - Updated with auth section
local-data.js    - Infrastructure config (48KB)
oauth-callback.html - OAuth callback page
script.js        - Compiled TypeScript (23KB)
styles.css       - Compiled SCSS (47KB)
```

You can now open `dist_vanilla/index.html` locally and manage your entire cloud infrastructure!

### 2. **New `/api/metrics/services` Endpoint** (lines 1185-1266)

**Gets metrics for ALL running containers** across all VMs:

    "container": "npm-app",
    "ram": 314572800,
    "storage": 524288000,
    "vram": 0
  }
]
```

**Features**:
- Parses Docker memory sizes (`MiB`, `GiB`) to bytes
- Matches containers to services by name
- Handles missing or unknown services gracefully

### 3. **New `/api/service/{id}/kill` Endpoint** (lines 1268-1314)

**Stops a Docker container** with GitHub OAuth authentication:

**Authentication**:
- Requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header
- Uses existing `verify_github_auth()` function (line 1588)
- Checks user against `GITHUB_ALLOWED_USERS`

**How it works**:
1. Verifies GitHub token
2. Looks up service in CONFIG
3. Finds which VM runs the service
4. Gets container name
5. Executes `sudo docker stop {container_name}` via SSH
6. Returns success/error with audit trail

**Request**:
```bash
POST /api/service/matomo-app/kill
Authorization: Bearer ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

**Success Response**:

### Issue Resolved
The metrics were returning `null` because the Docker container couldn't access the SSH keys to query the remote VMs. The problem was a **UID mismatch** - the container's `appuser` (UID 1000) couldn't read the `/home/ubuntu/.ssh` directory owned by UID 1001.

- **Percentage** on bottom right (e.g., "45%")

- Rename container `matomo-db` → `analytics-db`

Network Architecture\n   344→\n   345→### 5.1 Traffic Flow\n   346→\n   347→```\n   348→+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+\n   349→|                              INTERNET                                    |\n   350→|    HTTP(80) | HTTPS(443) | SSH(22) | SMTP(25,587) | IMAP(993)           |\n   351→+------+------+------+------+----+----+------+-------+------+--------------+\n   352→       |            |           |           |              |\n   353→       v            v           v           v              v\n   354→+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+\n   355→|                    UFW FIREWALL (Default: DROP)                          |\n   356→|   OK: 22/tcp  OK: 80/tcp  OK: 443/tcp  OK: 25/tcp  OK: 587/tcp          |\n   357→|   OK: 993/tcp  BLOCKED: 8080  BLOCKED: 3306  BLOCKED: 5432              |\n   358→+------+----------------+----------+----------------+----------------------+\n   359→       |                |          |                |\n   360→       |                v          |                v\n   361→       |      +-----------------+  |      +-----------------+\n   362→       |      |  NGINX PROXY    |  |      |   MAIL SERVER   |\n   363→       |      |  (Host Level)   |  |      |   (Docker)      |\n   364→       |      |  Listen: 80,443 |  |      |   Listen: 25,   |\n   365→       |      +--------+--------+  |      |   587, 993      |\n   366→       |               |           |      +-----------------+\n   367→       |               v           |\n   368→       |      +--------------------------------------+\n   369→       |      |         DOCKER ENVIRONMENT          |\n   370→       |      |  +------------+  +------------+     |\n   371→       |      |  | PUBLIC     |  | PRIVATE    |     |\n   372→       |      |  | NETWORK    |  | NETWORK    |     |\n   373→       |      |  | :8080      |  | :8082      |     |\n   374→       |      |  | :8081      |  | internal   |     |\n   375→       |      |  +------------+  +------------+     |\n   376→       |      +--------------------------------------+\n   377→       |\n   378→       v\n   379→+-----------------+\n   380→|   HOST OS       |\n   381→|   (SSH Direct)  |\n   382→|   Ubuntu 24.04  |\n   383→+-----------------+\n   384→```\n   385→\n   386→### 5.2 External Ports (Internet-Facing)\n   387→\n   388→| Port | Protocol | Service | VM |\n   389→|------|----------|---------|-----|\n   390→| 22 | TCP | SSH | All |\n   391→| 80 | TCP | HTTP (redirect to HTTPS) | All |\n   392→| 443 | TCP | HTTPS | All |\n   393→| 81 | TCP | NPM Admin | Web Server 1, Services Server 1 |\n   394→| 22000 | TCP | Syncthing Sync | Web Server 1 |\n   395→| 21027 | UDP | Syncthing Discovery | Web Server 1 |\n   396→\n   397→### 5.3 Internal Ports (localhost only, proxied via NPM)\n   398→\n   399→| Port | Service | VM |\n   400→|------|---------|-----|\n   401→| 8080 | Matomo | Web Server 1 |\n   402→| 8384 | Syncthing GUI | Web Server 1 |\n   403→| 5678 | n8n | Services Server 1 |\n   404→| 3306 | MariaDB | Web Server 1 |\n   405→\n   406→### 5.4 Key Design Decisions\n   407→\n   408→1. **NGINX on Host (not Docker)**\n   409→   - SSL termination at host level\n   410→   - Direct access to Let\'s Encrypt\n   411→   - Survives container restarts\n   412→\n   413→2. **Localhost Binding**\n   414→   - All containers bind to `127.0.0.1:port`\n   415→   - Prevents Docker UFW bypass vulnerability\n   416→   - Internet cannot reach containers directly\n   417→\n   418→3. **SSH Direct Path**\n   419→   - SSH bypasses NGINX and Docker\n   420→   - Direct access to host OS\n   421→   - Emergency access even if containers fail\n   422→\n   423→---\n   424→\n   425→## 6. Docker Network Isolation\n   426→\n   427→### 6.1 Network Topology\n   428→\n   429→```yaml\n   430→networks:\n   431→  # Public services - internet accessible via NGINX\n   432→  public_net:\n   433→    driver: bridge\n   434→    subnet: 172.20.0.0/24\n   435→    purpose: Public services accessible via NGINX\n   436→\n   437→  # Private services - requires authentication\n   438→  private_net:\n   439→    driver: bridge\n   440→    internal: true  # No external access\n   441→    subnet: 172.21.0.0/24\n   442→    purpose: Private services requiring authentication\n   443→\n   444→  # Mail services - isolated email stack\n   445→  mail_net:\n   446→    driver: bridge\n   447→    subnet: 172.22.0.0/24\n   448→    purpose: Isolated email stack\n   449→\n   450→  # Database bridge - backup agent only\n   451→  db_bridge:\n   452→    driver: bridge\n   453→    internal: true\n   454→    subnet: 172.23.0.0/24\n   455→    purpose: Database backup agent access\n   456→```\n   457→\n   458→### 6.2 Network Membership Matrix\n   459→\n   460→| Container | public_net | private_net | mail_net | db_bridge |\n   461→|-----------|:----------:|:-----------:|:--------:|:---------:|\n   462→| web-server | X | | | |\n   463→| matomo-app | X | | | |\n   464→| matomo-db | X | | | X |\n   465→| nextcloud-app | | X | | |\n   466→| nextcloud-db | | X | | X |\n   467→| redis | | X | | |\n   468→| mailserver | | | X | |\n   469→| mail-db | | | X | X |\n   470→| backup-agent | | | | X |\n   471→\n   472→### 6.3 Isolation Verification\n   473→\n   474→```bash\n   475→# From matomo-app, verify cannot reach private network\n   476→docker exec matomo-app ping -c 1 172.21.0.2  # Should fail\n   477→\n   478→# From nextcloud-app, verify cannot reach public network\n   479→docker exec nextcloud-app ping -c 1 172.20.0.2  # Should fail\n   480→\n   481→# Verify internal network has no external access\n   482→docker exec nextcloud-db curl -s http://google.com  # Should fail\n   483→```\n   484→\n   485→---\n   486→\n   487→## 7. Security Architecture\n   488→\n   489→### 7.1 Architecture Philosophy\n   490→\n   491→**"Blast Radius Containment"** - Assume any public-facing service can be compromised. Design the infrastructure so that a breach in one service cannot spread to others.\n   492→\n   493→### 7.2 Defense in Depth Model\n   494→\n   495→```\n   496→Layer 1: Network Edge\n   497→├── Oracle Cloud Security Lists\n   498→├── UFW Firewall (host level)\n   499→└── Fail2Ban (brute force protection)\n   500→\n   501→Layer 2: Traffic Routing\n   502→├── NGINX TLS termination\n   503→├── HTTP → HTTPS redirect\n   504→├── Rate limiting\n   505→└── Security headers\n   506→\n   507→Layer 3: Application Isolation\n   508→├── Docker networks (no cross-talk)\n   509→├── Container user namespaces\n   510→├── Read-only filesystems\n   511→└── Resource limits (CPU, memory)\n   512→\n   513→Layer 4: Data Protection\n   514→├── Separate volumes per service\n   515→├── LUKS encryption at rest\n   516→├── Database per service\n   517→└── Backup encryption\n   518→```\n   519→\n   520→### 7.3 UFW Configuration\n   521→\n   522→```bash\n   523→# Reset to defaults\n   524→sudo ufw --force reset\n   525→sudo ufw default deny incoming\n   526→sudo ufw default allow outgoing\n   527→\n   528→# Allow specific ports\n   529→sudo ufw allow 22/tcp comment \'SSH\'\n   530→sudo ufw allow 80/tcp comment \'HTTP redirect\'\n   531→sudo ufw allow 443/tcp comment \'HTTPS\'\n   532→sudo ufw allow 25/tcp comment \'SMTP\'\n   533→sudo ufw allow 587/tcp comment \'SMTP Submission\'\n   534→sudo ufw allow 993/tcp comment \'IMAPS\'\n   535→\n   536→# Enable firewall\n   537→sudo ufw enable\n   538→sudo ufw status verbose\n   539→```\n   540→\n   541→### 7.4 SSH Hardening\n   542→\n   543→```bash\n   544→# /etc/ssh/sshd_config\n   545→PermitRootLogin no\n   546→PasswordAuthentication no\n   547→PubkeyAuthentication yes\n   548→MaxAuthTries 3\n   549→AllowUsers ubuntu\n   550→```\n   551→\n   552→### 7.5 NGINX Security Headers\n   553→\n   554→```nginx\n   555→# /etc/nginx/conf.d/security.conf\n   556→add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;\n   557→add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;\n   558→add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;\n   559→add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always;\n   560→add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;\n   561→```\n   562→\n   563→### 7.6 Docker Hardening\n   564→\n   565→```yaml\n   566→services:\n   567→  web-server:\n   568→    security_opt:\n   569→      - no-new-privileges:true\n   570→    read_only: true\n   571→    tmpfs:\n   572→      - /tmp\n   573→    deploy:\n   574→      resources:\n   575→        limits:\n   576→          cpus: \'0.5\'\n   577→          memory: 256M\n   578→```\n   579→\n   580→---\n   581→\n   582→## 8. Volume & Storage Strategy\n   583→\n   584→### 8.1 Storage Partitions (ARM Server - Future)\n   585→\n   586→```\n   587→Host Filesystem:\n   588→├── / (Boot Volume - 47GB)\n   589→│   ├── /etc/nginx/          # NGINX configs\n   590→│   ├── /opt/docker/         # Docker compose files\n   591→│   └── /home/ubuntu/        # User home\n   592→│\n   593→├── /mnt/public (Block Volume 1 - 50GB)\n   594→│   ├── matomo-db/           # MariaDB data\n   595→│   ├── matomo-files/        # Matomo uploads\n   596→│   └── web-static/          # Static website files\n   597→│\n   598→├── /mnt/private (Block Volume 2 - 50GB) [LUKS ENCRYPTED]\n   599→│   ├── nextcloud-db/        # PostgreSQL data\n   600→│   ├── nextcloud-files/     # User files\n   601→│   └── redis-data/          # Persistent cache\n   602→│\n   603→└── /mnt/mail (Block Volume 3 - 50GB) [LUKS ENCRYPTED]\n   604→    ├── mailboxes/           # Maildir storage\n   605→    ├── mail-config/         # Server configuration\n   606→    └── dkim-keys/           # DKIM signing keys\n   607→```\n   608→\n   609→### 8.2 LUKS Encryption Setup\n   610→\n   611→```bash\n   612→# Create encrypted partition\n   613→sudo cryptsetup luksFormat /dev/sdb1\n   614→sudo cryptsetup open /dev/sdb1 private_crypt\n   615→\n   616→# Format and mount\n   617→sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/mapper/private_crypt\n   618→sudo mount /dev/mapper/private_crypt /mnt/private\n   619→\n   620→# Auto-unlock at boot (with keyfile)\n   621→sudo dd if=/dev/urandom of=/root/.luks-keyfile bs=4096 count=1\n   622→sudo chmod 400 /root/.luks-keyfile\n   623→sudo cryptsetup luksAddKey /dev/sdb1 /root/.luks-keyfile\n   624→\n   625→# /etc/crypttab\n   626→private_crypt /dev/sdb1 /root/.luks-keyfile luks\n   627→```\n   628→\n   629→---\n   630→\n   631→## 9. Database Strategy\n   632→\n   633→### 9.1 SQL vs NoSQL Decision Matrix\n   634→\n   635→| Use Case | Type | Database | Reason |\n   636→|----------|------|----------|--------|\n   637→| Analytics (Matomo) | SQL | MariaDB | Complex queries, time-series |\n   638→| User Files (NextCloud) | SQL | PostgreSQL | Metadata, relations |\n   639→| Mail Accounts | SQL | SQLite | Simple, lightweight |\n   640→| Session Cache | NoSQL | Redis | Fast, ephemeral |\n   641→| Search Index | NoSQL | Redis | Key-value lookups |\n   642→| Email Storage | Files | Maildir | Standard format |\n   643→\n   644→### 9.2 Isolation Rule\n   645→\n   646→```\n   647→+-------------------------------------------------------------+\n   648→|                    RULE: ONE DB PER SERVICE                  |\n   649→|                                                              |\n   650→|  WRONG: Single MariaDB for Matomo + NextCloud               |\n   651→|  RIGHT: Separate MariaDB (Matomo) + PostgreSQL (NC)         |\n   652→|                                                              |\n   653→|  Reason: Prevents privilege escalation between services     |\n   654→+-------------------------------------------------------------+\n   655→```\n   656→\n   657→---\n   658→\n   659→## 10. SSH & Access Commands\n   660→\n   661→### 10.1 SSH Access\n   662→\n   663→```bash\n   664→# Oracle Web Server 1 (Matomo, Syncthing)\n   665→ssh ubuntu@130.110.251.193\n   666→\n   667→# Oracle Services Server 1 (n8n)\n   668→ssh ubuntu@129.151.228.66\n   669→\n   670→# Google Cloud (when active)\n   671→gcloud compute ssh arch-1 --zone us-central1-a\n   672→```\n   673→\n   674→### 10.2 Docker Commands (after SSH)\n   675→\n   676→```bash\n   677→# View all containers\n   678→sudo docker ps\n   679→\n   680→# View logs\n   681→sudo docker logs --tail 100 matomo-app\n   682→sudo docker logs --tail 100 -f matomo-db\n   683→\n   684→# Execute shell in container\n   685→sudo docker exec -it matomo-app bash\n   686→sudo docker exec -it matomo-db bash\n   687→sudo docker exec -it syncthing sh\n   688→sudo docker exec -it n8n sh\n   689→\n   690→# Restart container\n   691→sudo docker restart matomo-app\n   692→\n   693→# View resource usage\n   694→sudo docker stats --no-stream\n   695→```\n   696→\n   697→### 10.3 System Commands\n   698→\n   699→```bash\n   700→# Disk usage\n   701→df -h\n   702→\n   703→# Memory usage\n   704→free -h\n   705→\n   706→# Check swap\n   707→swapon --show\n   708→\n   709→# Create swap (if needed - for 1GB VMs)\n   710→sudo fallocate -l 1G /swapfile\n   711→sudo chmod 600 /swapfile\n   712→sudo mkswap /swapfile\n   713→sudo swapon /swapfile\n   714→echo \'/swapfile none swap sw 0 0\' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab\n   715→```\n   716→\n   717→---\n   718→\n   719→## 11. Operations & Maintenance\n   840→\n   841→### 12.1 Daily Operations\n   842→\n   843→```bash\n   844→# Check service health\n   845→docker ps --format "table {{.Names}}\\t{{.Status}}\\t{{.Ports}}"\n   846→\n   847→# View logs\n   848→docker logs --tail 100 matomo-app\n   849→docker logs --tail 100 -f mailserver\n   850→\n   851→# Check disk usage\n   852→df -h /mnt/*\n   853→docker system df\n   854→```\n   855→\n   856→### 12.2 Weekly Operations\n   857→\n   858→```bash\n   859→# Update containers\n   860→docker compose pull\n   861→docker compose up -d\n   862→\n   863→# Clean old images\n   864→docker image prune -a --filter "until=168h"\n   865→\n   866→# Verify backups\n   867→ls -la /backup/\n   868→```\n   869→\n   870→### 12.3 Monthly Operations\n   871→\n   872→```bash\n   873→# OS updates\n   874→sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y\n   875→\n   876→# SSL certificate check\n   877→sudo certbot certificates\n   878→\n   879→# Review firewall rules\n   880→sudo ufw status verbose\n   881→\n   882→# Audit Docker networks\n   883→docker network ls\n   884→docker network inspect public_net\n   885→```\n   886→\n   887→### 12.4 Dashboard Usage\n   888→\n   889→The unified `cloud-dashboard.py` provides three modes: TUI, API Server, and CLI.\n   890→\n   891→```bash\n   892→# Launch interactive TUI dashboard\n   893→python cloud-dashboard.py\n   894→\n   895→# Start Flask API server (for web dashboard)\n   896→python cloud-dashboard.py serve\n   897→python cloud-dashboard.py serve --debug\n   898→\n   899→# Quick CLI status check\n   900→python cloud-dashboard.py status\n   901→\n   902→# Help\n   903→python cloud-dashboard.py help\n   904→```\n   905→\n   906→#### API Endpoints (when running `serve`)\n   907→\n   908→| Endpoint | Description |\n   909→|----------|-------------|\n   910→| `GET /api/health` | API health check |\n   911→| `GET /api/vms` | List all VMs |\n   912→| `GET /api/vms/<id>` | Get VM details |\n   913→| `GET /api/vms/<id>/status` | VM health status (ping, SSH) |\n   914→| `GET /api/vms/<id>/containers` | Docker containers on VM |\n   915→| `GET /api/services` | List all services |\n   916→| `GET /api/services/<id>` | Get service details |\n   917→| `GET /api/services/<id>/status` | Service health status (HTTP check) |\n   918→| `GET /api/dashboard/summary` | Full dashboard with health checks |\n   919→| `GET /api/dashboard/quick-status` | Quick status (config only, no checks) |\n   920→| `GET /api/config` | Full JSON configuration |\n   921→| `POST /api/config/reload` | Reload configuration from disk |\n   922→\n   923→#### TUI Commands\n   924→\n   925→| Key | Action |\n   926→|-----|--------|\n   927→| `1` | VM Details |\n   928→| `2` | Container Status |\n   929→| `3` | Reboot VM |\n   930→| `4` | Restart Container |\n   931→| `5` | View Logs |\n   932→| `6` | Stop/Start Container |\n   933→| `7` | SSH to VM |\n   934→| `8` | Open URL |\n   935→| `S` | Quick Status |\n   936→| `R` | Refresh |\n   937→| `Q` | Quit |\n   938→\n   939→### 12.5 Incident Response\n   940→\n   941→**If container compromised**:\n   942→```bash\n   943→# 1. Isolate container\n   944→docker network disconnect public_net compromised-container\n   945→docker stop compromised-container\n   946→\n   947→# 2. Preserve evidence\n   948→docker commit compromised-container evidence:$(date +%s)\n   949→docker logs compromised-container > /tmp/incident-logs.txt\n   950→\n   951→# 3. Restore from backup\n   952→docker compose down compromised-service\n   953→rm -rf /mnt/public/compromised-data/*\n   954→# Restore from backup...\n   955→docker compose up -d compromised-service\n   956→\n   957→# 4. Post-incident\n   958→# - Review logs\n   959→# - Update passwords\n   960→# - Patch vulnerabilities\n   961→# - Update monitoring\n   962→```\n   963→\n   964→---\n   965→\n   966→## 12A. $1.25/1M | $5.00/1M | $0.31/1M | - |\n  1171→| **Google** | Gemini Pro 3.0 | $1.25/1M | $5.00/1M | $0.31/1M | - |\n  1172→\n  1173→**Data Flow (Simplified):**\n  1174→```\n  1175→~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl\n  1176→    │\n  1177→    └── ccusage CLI (npm package) ← Use directly, no wrapper needed!\n  1178→            │\n  1179→            └── cloud_dash.py calls subprocess.run([\'ccusage\', ...])\n  1180→                    │\n  1181→                    └── /api/costs/ai/* endpoints\n  1182→```\n  1183→\n  1184→**ccusage Commands (all support --json):**\n  1185→```bash\n  1186→ccusage blocks -a --json      # Current 5h block with projections, burn rate\n  1187→ccusage daily --json -b       # Daily breakdown with model costs\n  1188→ccusage monthly --json -b     # Monthly totals with model breakdown\n  1189→ccusage weekly --json -b      # Weekly aggregation\n  1190→ccusage session --json        # Per-conversation breakdown\n  1191→ccusage blocks --live         # Real-time TUI monitoring\n  1192→```\n  1193→\n  1194→**API Endpoints (direct ccusage integration):**\n  1195→```\n  1196→GET /api/costs/ai/now      → ccusage blocks -a --json\n  1197→GET /api/costs/ai/daily    → ccusage daily --json -b\n  1198→GET /api/costs/ai/monthly  → ccusage monthly --json -b\n  1199→GET /api/costs/ai/weekly   → ccusage weekly --json -b\n  1200→```\n  1201→\n  1202→**Flask Implementation (simple subprocess):**\n  1203→```python\n  1204→import subprocess, json\n  1205→\n  1206→@app.route(\'/api/costs/ai/now\')\n  1207→def api_costs_ai_now():\n  1208→    result = subprocess.run([\'ccusage\', \'blocks\', \'-a\', \'--json\'],\n  1209→                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)\n  1210→    return jsonify(json.loads(result.stdout))\n  1211→\n  1212→@app.route(\'/api/costs/ai/daily\')\n  1213→def api_costs_ai_daily():\n  1214→    result = subprocess.run([\'ccusage\', \'daily\', \'--json\', \'-b\'],\n  1215→                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)\n  1216→    return jsonify(json.loads(result.stdout))\n  1217→```\n  1218→\n  1219→**UI Components:**\n  1220→- Current 5h window: Usage bar, token breakdown, burn rate\n  1221→- Budget tracker: MTD vs limit, projected EOM cost\n  1222→- Model distribution: Pie chart (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus %)\n  1223→- Daily trend: Sparkline of cost over time\n  1224→- Alerts: Warning when Opus > 10%, budget > 75%\n  1225→\n  1226→### 12A.6 Dashboard Tab Structure\n  1227→\n  1228→```\n Authentication & Admin API\n  1351→\n  1352→### 14.1 Overview\n  1353→\n  1354→The dashboard supports **GitHub OAuth 2.0** authentication for admin operations. Public endpoints (status, health) remain unauthenticated. Admin endpoints (reboot, restart, stop/start) require login.\n  1355→\n  1356→### 14.2 Authentication Flow\n  1357→\n  1358→```\n  1359→+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+\n  1360→|   Dashboard UI   |     |   Flask API      |     |   GitHub OAuth   |\n  1361→+--------+---------+     +--------+---------+     +--------+---------+\n  1362→         |                        |                        |\n  1363→         | 1. Click "Login"       |                        |\n  1364→         |----------------------->|                        |\n  1365→         |                        | 2. Redirect to GitHub  |\n  1366→         |                        |----------------------->|\n  1367→         |                        |                        |\n  1368→         |                        | 3. User authorizes     |\n  1369→         |                        |<-----------------------|\n  1370→         |                        |                        |\n  1371→         | 4. Return JWT token    |                        |\n  1372→         |<-----------------------|                        |\n  1373→         |                        |                        |\n  1374→         | 5. Admin commands      |                        |\n  1375→         | (with Bearer token)    |                        |\n  1376→         |----------------------->|                        |\n  1377→         |                        |                        |\n  1378→```\n  1379→\n  1380→### 14.3 Endpoint Access Levels\n  1381→\n  1382→| Access Level | Endpoints | Auth Required |\n  1383→|--------------|-----------|---------------|\n  1384→| **Public** | `/api/health`, `/api/vms`, `/api/services`, `/api/dashboard/*` | No |\n  1385→| **Admin** | `/api/admin/vms/*/reboot`, `/api/admin/vms/*/containers/*/restart` | Yes (JWT) |\n  1386→\n  1387→### 14.4 Admin API Endpoints\n  1388→\n  1389→| Endpoint | Method | Description | Auth |\n  1390→|----------|--------|-------------|------|\n  1391→| `POST /api/auth/github` | POST | Initiate GitHub OAuth flow | No |\n  1392→| `GET /api/auth/callback` | GET | GitHub OAuth callback | No |\n  1393→| `GET /api/auth/me` | GET | Get current user info | Yes |\n  1394→| `POST /api/auth/logout` | POST | Invalidate session | Yes |\n  1395→| `POST /api/admin/vms/<id>/reboot` | POST | Reboot VM via SSH | Yes |\n  1396→| `POST /api/admin/vms/<id>/containers/<name>/restart` | POST | Restart Docker container | Yes |\n  1397→| `POST /api/admin/vms/<id>/containers/<name>/stop` | POST | Stop Docker container | Yes |\n  1398→| `POST /api/admin/vms/<id>/containers/<name>/start` | POST | Start Docker container | Yes |\n  1399→| `POST /api/admin/services/<id>/restart` | POST | Restart service (container) | Yes |\n  1400→\n  1401→### 14.5 GitHub OAuth Configuration\n  1402→\n  1403→```bash\n  1404→# Required environment variables\n  1405→GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id\n  1406→GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret\n  1407→JWT_SECRET_KEY=your_jwt_secret\n  1408→ALLOWED_GITHUB_USERS=diegonmarcos  # Comma-separated usernames\n  1409→```\n  1410→\n  1411→GitHub App settings:\n  1412→- **Authorization callback URL**: `https://cloud.diegonmarcos.com/api/auth/callback`\n  1413→- **Scopes**: `read:user` (only need username verification)\n  1414→\n  1415→### 14.6 Dashboard UI Changes\n  1416→\n  1417→**Before Login:**\n  1418→```\n  1419→+------------------------------------------+\n  1420→|  Cloud Dashboard            [Login] btn  |\n  1421→+------------------------------------------+\n  1422→|  VMs        | Services                   |\n  1423→|  - Status   | - Status                   |\n  1424→|  (read-only)| (read-only)                |\n  1425→+------------------------------------------+\n  1426→```\n  1427→\n  1428→**After Login:**\n  1429→```\n  1430→+------------------------------------------+\n  1431→|  Cloud Dashboard    [diego] [Logout] btn |\n  1432→+------------------------------------------+\n  1433→|  VMs                | Services           |\n  1434→|  - Status           | - Status           |\n  1435→|  - [Reboot] btn     | - [Restart] btn    |\n  1436→|  - [Containers]     | - [Stop/Start]     |\n  1437→|    - [Restart]      |                    |\n  1438→|    - [Stop/Start]   |                    |\n  1439→+------------------------------------------+\n  1440→```\n  1441→\n  1442→### 14.7 Security Considerations\n  1443→\n  1444→1. **JWT Expiration**: Tokens expire after 24 hours\n  1445→2. **Username Whitelist**: Only `ALLOWED_GITHUB_USERS` can access admin endpoints\n  1446→3. **HTTPS Only**: OAuth flow requires HTTPS\n  1447→4. **CSRF Protection**: State parameter in OAuth flow\n  1448→5. **Rate Limiting**: Admin endpoints rate-limited to prevent abuse\n  1449→6. **Audit Logging**: All admin actions logged with timestamp and user\n  1450→\n  1451→### 14.8 Implementation Status\n  1452→\n  1453→| Component | Status |\n  1454→|-----------|--------|\n  1455→| GitHub OAuth flow | `dev` |\n  1456→| JWT token generation | `dev` |\n  1457→| Admin endpoints | `dev` |\n  1458→| Dashboard UI (login button) | `dev` |\n  1459→| Dashboard UI (admin controls) | `dev` |\n  1460→\n  1461→---\n  1462→\n  1463→## Changelog\n  1464→\n  1465→| Date | Change |\n  1620→\n  1621→## 15. Dashboard Architecture\n  1622→\n  1623→### 15.1 Overview\n  1624→\n  1625→The Cloud Dashboard consists of three main components:\n  1626→\n  1627→| Component | Technology | Location | Purpose |\n  1628→|-----------|------------|----------|---------|\n  1629→| **cloud-app** | HTML/CSS/JS | GitHub Pages | Static frontend UI |\n  1630→| **flask-app** | Python Flask | Oracle VM | REST API + OAuth |\n  1631→| **cloud_dash.json** | JSON | Oracle VM | Infrastructure data |\n  1632→\n  1633→### 15.2 Frontend-to-API Integration\n  1634→\n  1635→The frontend HTML fetches all data dynamically from the Flask API via JavaScript:\n  1636→\n  1637→```javascript\n  1638→// Frontend JavaScript (cloud_dash.html)\n  1639→\n  1640→// 1. Fetch VM list on page load\n  1641→async function loadVMs() {\n  1642→    const response = await fetch(\'https://cloud.diegonmarcos.com/api/vms\');\n  1643→    const vms = await response.json();\n  1644→    renderVMTable(vms);\n  1645→}\n  1646→\n  1647→// 2. Fetch live status for each VM\n  1648→async function checkVMStatus(vmId) {\n  1649→    const response = await fetch(`https://cloud.diegonmarcos.com/api/vms/${vmId}/status`);\n  1650→    const status = await response.json();\n  1651→    updateStatusIndicator(vmId, status);\n  1652→}\n  1653→\n  1654→// 3. Admin actions (requires OAuth token)\n  1655→async function rebootVM(vmId) {\n  1656→    const token = localStorage.getItem(\'github_token\');\n  1657→    const response = await fetch(`https://cloud.diegonmarcos.com/api/vm/${vmId}/reboot`, {\n  1658→        method: \'POST\',\n  1659→        headers: { \'Authorization\': `Bearer ${token}` }\n  1660→    });\n  1661→    return response.json();\n  1662→}\n  1663→```\n  1664→\n  1665→### 15.3 API Endpoint → Frontend Mapping\n  1666→\n  1667→| Frontend Feature | API Endpoint | Data Used |\n  1668→|------------------|--------------|-----------|\n  1669→| VM Table | `GET /api/vms` | name, IP, status, services |\n  1670→| VM Status Indicators | `GET /api/vms/<id>/status` | ping, ssh, uptime |\n  1671→| Service Cards | `GET /api/services` | name, URL, status |\n  1672→| Service Health | `GET /api/services/<id>/status` | http_check, response_time |\n  1673→| Reboot Button | `POST /api/vm/<id>/reboot` | success/error message |\n  1674→| Login State | `GET /api/auth/me` | username, avatar |\n  1675→\n  1676→### 15.4 Architecture Visualization Pages\n  1677→\n  1678→The dashboard includes pages that render Mermaid diagrams from the spec files:\n  1679→\n  1680→| Page | Source | Content |\n  1681→|------|--------|---------|\n  1682→| `arch.html` | Cloud-spec_Tables.md (Mermaid) | Infrastructure tree diagram |\n  1683→| `ai-arch.html` | Cloud-spec_Tables.md (Mermaid) | AI services architecture |\n  1684→\n  1685→**Rendering Process:**\n  1686→1. Mermaid code is authored in `Cloud-spec_Tables.md` (source of truth)\n  1687→2. HTML pages include Mermaid.js library\n  1688→3. Mermaid code is embedded in `<pre class="mermaid">` blocks\n  1689→4. Mermaid.js renders SVG diagrams at runtime\n  1690→\n  1691→---\n  1692→\n  1693→## 16. USER (line 4479):

why you need to send emails using 25? cant you use ogher?

----------------------------------------
ASSISTANT (line 4481):
----------------------------------------
Good question! Here's the port breakdown:

| Port | Direction | Purpose |
|------|-----------|---------|
| **25** | **INBOUND** | Other mail servers connect TO you (required to **receive** email) |
| 587 | OUTBOUND | Your server sends TO relays (submission) |
| 465 | OUTBOUND | Secure SMTP sending |
| 993 | INBOUND | IMAP - reading your mailbox |

**The problem:** To receive email from Gmail, Yahoo, etc., their servers need to connect to YOUR port 25. Oracle blocks this to prevent spam.

**Your current setup actually works:**
- **Receive**: Gmail handles it (MX → smtp.google.com)
- **Send**: Gmail SMTP relay (port 587 outbound) - already configured for Authelia

You don't need a self-hosted mail server because:
1. Gmail receives mail at `me@diegonmarcos.com`
2. Gmail relay sends mail for Authelia/apps

The self-hosted mail server would only add complexity. Your email is already working via Gmail.

so cloudfre can get my emails at port 25 and then redirect to my whatever port?

ASSISTANT (line 4501):

**Not exactly** - Cloudflare Email Routing works like this:

```
[Sender] → port 25 → [Cloudflare] → forwards to → [Another EMAIL address]
                                                    (not custom port)
```

**What Cloudflare CAN do:**
- ✅ Receive on port 25
- ✅ Forward to another email (Gmail, ProtonMail, etc.)
- ✅ Email Workers (code that processes emails → can call your API via HTTPS)

**What Cloudflare CANNOT do:**
- ❌ Forward raw SMTP to your server on port 587/993
- ❌ Act as SMTP proxy to custom port

**For full self-hosted mail, you need:**

| Solution | How it works |
|----------|--------------|
| **Cloudflare + Email Worker** | CF receives → Worker calls your HTTPS API → your server stores email |
| **Mailgun Inbound** | MG receives on 25 → forwards via webhook (HTTP POST) to your server |
| **VPS with port 25** | Direct SMTP, no relay needed |

**Simplest path to replace Gmail:**
1. Cloudflare Email Routing → forward to a self-hosted mailbox (like Stalwart, Maddy) 
2. Your server only needs HTTPS (443) for the Worker webhook
3. Send outbound via Gmail relay (already configured)

Want to try the Cloudflare + Email Worker approach?

Principals in Stalwart follow the JMAP Sharing specification (as outlined in the RFC), which provides a standardized way to define and share resources among users. Each principal type represents a different category of entity and serves a distinct function within the system.\n\n### Individual Principal (User Accounts)\nThe Individual principal type in Stalwart represents a single person or user account. It is the fundamental unit for user management, as each email user within the system is stored as an individual principal. Individual principals contain all the information necessary to manage and authenticate a user\'s account, such as login credentials, email addresses, group memberships, and permissions.\n\nKey fields for individual principals:\n- **name**: This field represents the login name or username of the account. Groups function similarly to regular accounts in that they can receive emails, but they differ in a few important ways: group accounts cannot log in to the mail server using IMAP, POP3, or JMAP.\n- **Domain**: Represents a local domain managed by the mail server. Domain principals are crucial for defining the domains that the mail server recognizes as part of its local configuration. If a domain principal is not created for a specific domain, Stalwart will treat that domain as external and will not accept email delivery for it.\n- **API Key**: Used to grant external applications access to the management REST API or to register OAuth clients using the OAuth Dynamic Client Registration protocol.\n\n### Creating Accounts via Web UI\nOnce the domain and network are configured and verified it is time to create user accounts. what is the problem with creating a mail server that will be served ith fowarding emails from gogoel workspace account?

----------------------------------------
ASSISTANT (line 4619):
----------------------------------------
The problem is **Port 25 is blocked by Oracle Cloud**.

## How Email Forwarding Works

```
Gmail receives email → Gmail forwards to your server → Your server needs Port 25 OPEN
```

When Gmail (or any mail server) forwards an email, it connects to your server on **Port 25 (SMTP)**. This is how ALL mail servers talk to each other - it's the standard protocol.

## Your Situation

| What | Status |
|------|--------|
| Gmail receives emails | ✅ Works |
| Gmail tries to forward | ❌ Blocked |
| Port 25 on Oracle | 🚫 Closed by Oracle |

Oracle Cloud blocks port 25 on all VMs to prevent spam. You cannot receive forwarded emails directly.

## Solutions

1. **Cloudflare Email Routing** - Cloudflare receives on port 25, then forwards to your server on port 587 (which IS open)

2. **Pull instead of Push** - Use `fetchmail` or `imapsync` to PULL emails FROM Gmail to Stalwart (no port 25 needed)

3. **Different VPS provider** - Hetzner, OVH, Vultr allow port 25

4. **Request Oracle to unblock** - Submit a ticket (often denied)

---

**Simplest for now:** Use **fetchmail** to pull from Gmail IMAP every few minutes. Want me to set that up instead?

Network Architecture\n   344→\n   345→### 5.1 Traffic Flow\n   346→\n   347→```\n   348→+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+\n   349→|                              INTERNET                                    |\n   350→|    HTTP(80) | HTTPS(443) | SSH(22) | SMTP(25,587) | IMAP(993)           |\n   351→+------+------+------+------+----+----+------+-------+------+--------------+\n   352→       |            |           |           |              |\n   353→       v            v           v           v              v\n   354→+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+\n   355→|                    UFW FIREWALL (Default: DROP)                          |\n   356→|   OK: 22/tcp  OK: 80/tcp  OK: 443/tcp  OK: 25/tcp  OK: 587/tcp          |\n   357→|   OK: 993/tcp  BLOCKED: 8080  BLOCKED: 3306  BLOCKED: 5432              |\n   358→+------+----------------+----------+----------------+----------------------+\n   359→       |                |          |                |\n   360→       |                v          |                v\n   361→       |      +-----------------+  |      +-----------------+\n   362→       |      |  NGINX PROXY    |  |      |   MAIL SERVER   |\n   363→       |      |  (Host Level)   |  |      |   (Docker)      |\n   364→       |      |  Listen: 80,443 |  |      |   Listen: 25,   |\n   365→       |      +--------+--------+  |      |   587, 993      |\n   366→       |               |           |      +-----------------+\n   367→       |               v           |\n   368→       |      +--------------------------------------+\n   369→       |      |         DOCKER ENVIRONMENT          |\n   370→       |      |  +------------+  +------------+     |\n   371→       |      |  | PUBLIC     |  | PRIVATE    |     |\n   372→       |      |  | NETWORK    |  | NETWORK    |     |\n   373→       |      |  | :8080      |  | :8082      |     |\n   374→       |      |  | :8081      |  | internal   |     |\n   375→       |      |  +------------+  +------------+     |\n   376→       |      +--------------------------------------+\n   377→       |\n   378→       v\n   379→+-----------------+\n   380→|   HOST OS       |\n   381→|   (SSH Direct)  |\n   382→|   Ubuntu 24.04  |\n   383→+-----------------+\n   384→```\n   385→\n   386→### 5.2 External Ports (Internet-Facing)\n   387→\n   388→| Port | Protocol | Service | VM |\n   389→|------|----------|---------|-----|\n   390→| 22 | TCP | SSH | All |\n   391→| 80 | TCP | HTTP (redirect to HTTPS) | All |\n   392→| 443 | TCP | HTTPS | All |\n   393→| 81 | TCP | NPM Admin | Web Server 1, Services Server 1 |\n   394→| 22000 | TCP | Syncthing Sync | Web Server 1 |\n   395→| 21027 | UDP | Syncthing Discovery | Web Server 1 |\n   396→\n   397→### 5.3 Internal Ports (localhost only, proxied via NPM)\n   398→\n   399→| Port | Service | VM |\n   400→|------|---------|-----|\n   401→| 8080 | Matomo | Web Server 1 |\n   402→| 8384 | Syncthing GUI | Web Server 1 |\n   403→| 5678 | n8n | Services Server 1 |\n   404→| 3306 | MariaDB | Web Server 1 |\n   405→\n   406→### 5.4 Key Design Decisions\n   407→\n   408→1. **NGINX on Host (not Docker)**\n   409→   - SSL termination at host level\n   410→   - Direct access to Let\'s Encrypt\n   411→   - Survives container restarts\n   412→\n   413→2. **Localhost Binding**\n   414→   - All containers bind to `127.0.0.1:port`\n   415→   - Prevents Docker UFW bypass vulnerability\n   416→   - Internet cannot reach containers directly\n   417→\n   418→3. **SSH Direct Path**\n   419→   - SSH bypasses NGINX and Docker\n   420→   - Direct access to host OS\n   421→   - Emergency access even if containers fail\n   422→\n   423→---\n   424→\n   425→## 6. Docker Network Isolation\n   426→\n   427→### 6.1 Network Topology\n   428→\n   429→```yaml\n   430→networks:\n   431→  # Public services - internet accessible via NGINX\n   432→  public_net:\n   433→    driver: bridge\n   434→    subnet: 172.20.0.0/24\n   435→    purpose: Public services accessible via NGINX\n   436→\n   437→  # Private services - requires authentication\n   438→  private_net:\n   439→    driver: bridge\n   440→    internal: true  # No external access\n   441→    subnet: 172.21.0.0/24\n   442→    purpose: Private services requiring authentication\n   443→\n   444→  # Mail services - isolated email stack\n   445→  mail_net:\n   446→    driver: bridge\n   447→    subnet: 172.22.0.0/24\n   448→    purpose: Isolated email stack\n   449→\n   450→  # Database bridge - backup agent only\n   451→  db_bridge:\n   452→    driver: bridge\n   453→    internal: true\n   454→    subnet: 172.23.0.0/24\n   455→    purpose: Database backup agent access\n   456→```\n   457→\n   458→### 6.2 Network Membership Matrix\n   459→\n   460→| Container | public_net | private_net | mail_net | db_bridge |\n   461→|-----------|:----------:|:-----------:|:--------:|:---------:|\n   462→| web-server | X | | | |\n   463→| matomo-app | X | | | |\n   464→| matomo-db | X | | | X |\n   465→| nextcloud-app | | X | | |\n   466→| nextcloud-db | | X | | X |\n   467→| redis | | X | | |\n   468→| mailserver | | | X | |\n   469→| mail-db | | | X | X |\n   470→| backup-agent | | | | X |\n   471→\n   472→### 6.3 Isolation Verification\n   473→\n   474→```bash\n   475→# From matomo-app, verify cannot reach private network\n   476→docker exec matomo-app ping -c 1 172.21.0.2  # Should fail\n   477→\n   478→# From nextcloud-app, verify cannot reach public network\n   479→docker exec nextcloud-app ping -c 1 172.20.0.2  # Should fail\n   480→\n   481→# Verify internal network has no external access\n   482→docker exec nextcloud-db curl -s http://google.com  # Should fail\n   483→```\n   484→\n   485→---\n   486→\n   487→## 7. Security Architecture\n   488→\n   489→### 7.1 Architecture Philosophy\n   490→\n   491→**"Blast Radius Containment"** - Assume any public-facing service can be compromised. Design the infrastructure so that a breach in one service cannot spread to others.\n   492→\n   493→### 7.2 Defense in Depth Model\n   494→\n   495→```\n   496→Layer 1: Network Edge\n   497→├── Oracle Cloud Security Lists\n   498→├── UFW Firewall (host level)\n   499→└── Fail2Ban (brute force protection)\n   500→\n   501→Layer 2: Traffic Routing\n   502→├── NGINX TLS termination\n   503→├── HTTP → HTTPS redirect\n   504→├── Rate limiting\n   505→└── Security headers\n   506→\n   507→Layer 3: Application Isolation\n   508→├── Docker networks (no cross-talk)\n   509→├── Container user namespaces\n   510→├── Read-only filesystems\n   511→└── Resource limits (CPU, memory)\n   512→\n   513→Layer 4: Data Protection\n   514→├── Separate volumes per service\n   515→├── LUKS encryption at rest\n   516→├── Database per service\n   517→└── Backup encryption\n   518→```\n   519→\n   520→### 7.3 UFW Configuration\n   521→\n   522→```bash\n   523→# Reset to defaults\n   524→sudo ufw --force reset\n   525→sudo ufw default deny incoming\n   526→sudo ufw default allow outgoing\n   527→\n   528→# Allow specific ports\n   529→sudo ufw allow 22/tcp comment \'SSH\'\n   530→sudo ufw allow 80/tcp comment \'HTTP redirect\'\n   531→sudo ufw allow 443/tcp comment \'HTTPS\'\n   532→sudo ufw allow 25/tcp comment \'SMTP\'\n   533→sudo ufw allow 587/tcp comment \'SMTP Submission\'\n   534→sudo ufw allow 993/tcp comment \'IMAPS\'\n   535→\n   536→# Enable firewall\n   537→sudo ufw enable\n   538→sudo ufw status verbose\n   539→```\n   540→\n   541→### 7.4 SSH Hardening\n   542→\n   543→```bash\n   544→# /etc/ssh/sshd_config\n   545→PermitRootLogin no\n   546→PasswordAuthentication no\n   547→PubkeyAuthentication yes\n   548→MaxAuthTries 3\n   549→AllowUsers ubuntu\n   550→```\n   551→\n   552→### 7.5 NGINX Security Headers\n   553→\n   554→```nginx\n   555→# /etc/nginx/conf.d/security.conf\n   556→add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;\n   557→add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;\n   558→add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;\n   559→add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always;\n   560→add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;\n   561→```\n   562→\n   563→### 7.6 Docker Hardening\n   564→\n   565→```yaml\n   566→services:\n   567→  web-server:\n   568→    security_opt:\n   569→      - no-new-privileges:true\n   570→    read_only: true\n   571→    tmpfs:\n   572→      - /tmp\n   573→    deploy:\n   574→      resources:\n   575→        limits:\n   576→          cpus: \'0.5\'\n   577→          memory: 256M\n   578→```\n   579→\n   580→### 7.7 Security Services Inventory\n   581→\n   582→| Service | Type | Description | Location | Status |\n   583→|---------|------|-------------|----------|--------|\n   584→| **MyVault** | Password Manager | Bitwarden EU - Secure credential storage | vault.bitwarden.eu (SaaS) | ON |\n   585→| **Authelia** | 2FA Gateway | TOTP authentication for protected services (SMTP: Gmail) | GCP Micro 1 | ON |\n   586→| **OAuth2 Proxy** | Admin Auth | GitHub OAuth2 authentication proxy | GCP Micro 1 | ON |\n   587→| **NPM + SSL** | TLS Termination | Let\'s Encrypt certificates with auto-renewal | GCP Micro 1 | ON |\n   588→| **Docker Networks** | Network Isolation | Segmented: public_net, private_net, db_bridge | OCI Flex 1 | ON |\n   589→| **SSH Keys** | Access Control | Key-based auth for all VMs - no passwords | All VMs | ON |\n   590→| **Cloud Firewalls** | Network Security | OCI Security Lists + GCP Firewall Rules | OCI + GCP | ON |\n   591→| **Gmail SMTP Relay** | Email Notifications | App Password auth for Authelia notifications | Gmail (SaaS) | ON |\n   592→\n   593→### 7.8 Security Volume & Storage Strategy\n   636→\n   637→### 8.1 Storage Partitions (ARM Server - Future)\n   638→\n   639→```\n   640→Host Filesystem:\n   641→├── / (Boot Volume - 47GB)\n   642→│   ├── /etc/nginx/          # NGINX configs\n   643→│   ├── /opt/docker/         # Docker compose files\n   644→│   └── /home/ubuntu/        # User home\n   645→│\n   646→├── /mnt/public (Block Volume 1 - 50GB)\n   647→│   ├── matomo-db/           # MariaDB data\n   648→│   ├── matomo-files/        # Matomo uploads\n   649→│   └── web-static/          # Static website files\n   650→│\n   651→├── /mnt/private (Block Volume 2 - 50GB) [LUKS ENCRYPTED]\n   652→│   ├── nextcloud-db/        # PostgreSQL data\n   653→│   ├── nextcloud-files/     # User files\n   654→│   └── redis-data/          # Persistent cache\n   655→│\n   656→└── /mnt/mail (Block Volume 3 - 50GB) [LUKS ENCRYPTED]\n   657→    ├── mailboxes/           # Maildir storage\n   658→    ├── mail-config/         # Server configuration\n   659→    └── dkim-keys/           # DKIM signing keys\n   660→```\n   661→\n   662→### 8.2 LUKS Encryption Setup\n   663→\n   664→```bash\n   665→# Create encrypted partition\n   666→sudo cryptsetup luksFormat /dev/sdb1\n   667→sudo cryptsetup open /dev/sdb1 private_crypt\n   668→\n   669→# Format and mount\n   670→sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/mapper/private_crypt\n   671→sudo mount /dev/mapper/private_crypt /mnt/private\n   672→\n   673→# Auto-unlock at boot (with keyfile)\n   674→sudo dd if=/dev/urandom of=/root/.luks-keyfile bs=4096 count=1\n   675→sudo chmod 400 /root/.luks-keyfile\n   676→sudo cryptsetup luksAddKey /dev/sdb1 /root/.luks-keyfile\n   677→\n   678→# /etc/crypttab\n   679→private_crypt /dev/sdb1 /root/.luks-keyfile luks\n   680→```\n   681→\n   682→---\n   683→\n   684→## 9. Database Strategy\n   685→\n   686→### 9.1 SQL vs NoSQL Decision Matrix\n   687→\n   688→| Use Case | Type | Database | Reason |\n   689→|----------|------|----------|--------|\n   690→| Analytics (Matomo) | SQL | MariaDB | Complex queries, time-series |\n   691→| User Files (NextCloud) | SQL | PostgreSQL | Metadata, relations |\n   692→| Mail Accounts | SQL | SQLite | Simple, lightweight |\n   693→| Session Cache | NoSQL | Redis | Fast, ephemeral |\n   694→| Search Index | NoSQL | Redis | Key-value lookups |\n   695→| Email Storage | Files | Maildir | Standard format |\n   696→\n   697→### 9.2 Isolation Rule\n   698→\n   699→```\n   700→+-------------------------------------------------------------+\n   701→|                    RULE: ONE DB PER SERVICE                  |\n   702→|                                                              |\n   703→|  WRONG: Single MariaDB for Matomo + NextCloud               |\n   704→|  RIGHT: Separate MariaDB (Matomo) + PostgreSQL (NC)         |\n   705→|                                                              |\n   706→|  Reason: Prevents privilege escalation between services     |\n   707→+-------------------------------------------------------------+\n   708→```\n   709→\n   710→---\n   711→\n   712→## 10. SSH & Access Commands\n   713→\n   714→### 10.1 SSH Access\n   715→\n   716→```bash\n   717→# === OCI (Oracle Cloud) - Use SSH key ===\n   718→# Oracle Flex 1 - Main Services (Flask, Photos, n8n, Gitea)\n   719→ssh -i ~/Documents/Git/LOCAL_KEYS/00_terminal/ssh/id_rsa ubuntu@84.235.234.87\n   720→\n   721→# Oracle Micro 1 - Web Server (Matomo, Syncthing)\n   722→ssh -i ~/Documents/Git/LOCAL_KEYS/00_terminal/ssh/id_rsa ubuntu@130.110.251.193\n   723→\n   724→# Oracle Micro 2 - Services (n8n)\n   725→ssh -i ~/Documents/Git/LOCAL_KEYS/00_terminal/ssh/id_rsa ubuntu@129.151.228.66\n   726→\n   727→# === GCP (Google Cloud) - Use gcloud CLI ===\n   728→# GCP Micro 1 (arch-1) - NPM, Authelia, OAuth2 Proxy\n   729→gcloud compute ssh arch-1 --zone=us-central1-a\n   730→\n   731→# GCP with command execution\n   732→gcloud compute ssh arch-1 --zone=us-central1-a --command="sudo docker ps"\n   733→\n   734→# GCP copy file from container\n   735→gcloud compute ssh arch-1 --zone=us-central1-a --command="sudo docker cp npm:/data/database.sqlite /tmp/npm.db && sqlite3 /tmp/npm.db \'SELECT * FROM user;\'"\n   736→```\n   737→\n   738→### 10.1.1 GCP SSH Notes\n   739→- **DO NOT use `ssh user@IP` for GCP** - use `gcloud compute ssh` instead\n   740→- gcloud handles key exchange automatically via OS Login\n   741→- Instance name: `arch-1`, Zone: `us-central1-a`\n   742→- External IP: `34.55.55.234` (use gcloud, not direct SSH)\n   743→\n   744→### 10.2 Docker Commands (after SSH)\n   745→\n   746→```bash\n   747→# View all containers\n   748→sudo docker ps\n   749→\n   750→# View logs\n   751→sudo docker logs --tail 100 matomo-app\n   752→sudo docker logs --tail 100 -f matomo-db\n   753→\n   754→# Execute shell in container\n   755→sudo docker exec -it matomo-app bash\n   756→sudo docker exec -it matomo-db bash\n   757→sudo docker exec -it syncthing sh\n   758→sudo docker exec -it n8n sh\n   759→\n   760→# Restart container\n   761→sudo docker restart matomo-app\n   762→\n   763→# View resource usage\n   764→sudo docker stats --no-stream\n   765→```\n   766→\n   767→### 10.3 System Commands\n   768→\n   769→```bash\n   770→# Disk usage\n   771→df -h\n   772→\n   773→# Memory usage\n   774→free -h\n   775→\n   776→# Check swap\n   777→swapon --show\n   778→\n   779→# Create swap (if needed - for 1GB VMs)\n   780→sudo fallocate -l 1G /swapfile\n   781→sudo chmod 600 /swapfile\n   782→sudo mkswap /swapfile\n   783→sudo swapon /swapfile\n   784→echo \'/swapfile none swap sw 0 0\' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab\n   785→```\n   786→\n   787→---\n   788→\n   789→## 11.   794→\n   795→```\n   796→/front-Github_io/1.ops/\n   797→├── 0_Stack_Main.md           ← Technology stack & framework decisions\n   798→├── 1_Folder_Structure.md     ← Project structure & file 823→\n   824→- **Services list** → `services` object\n   825→- **VM cards** → `virtualMachines` object\n   826→- **Provider cards** → `providers` object\n   827→- **URLs & commands** → Each service/VM contains its URLs\n   828→- **Status indicators** → `status` field on each entity\n   829→\n   830→### 11.2 JSON Structure Overview\n   831→\n   832→```json\n   833→{\n   834→  "providers": {\n   835→    "oracle": { "consoleUrl": "...", "cli": {...} },\n   836→    "gcloud": { "consoleUrl": "...", "cli": {...} }\n   837→  },\n   838→  "vmCategories": {\n   839→    "services": { "name": "Services", {...}, "services": [...] },\n   844→    "oracle-services-server-1": { "ip": "...", "ssh": {...}, "services": [...] }\n   845→  },\n   846→  "serviceCategories": {\n   847→    "infra": { "name": "Infrastructure" },\n   848→    "productivity": { "name": "Productivity" },\n   849→    "web": { "name": "Web" },\n   850→    "ml": { "name": "Machine Learning" }\n   851→  },\n   852→  "services": {\n   853→    "matomo": { "urls": {...}, "docker": {...}, "status": "active" },\n   854→    "n8n": { "urls": {...}, "docker": {...}, "status": "active" }\n   855→  },\n   856→  "domains": { "primary": "diegonmarcos.com", "subdomains": {...} },\n   857→  "firewallRules": { "oracle-web-server-1": [...] }\n   858→}\n   859→```\n   860→\n   861→### 11.3 TypeScript Types (suggested)\n   862→\n Operations & Maintenance\n   910→\n   911→### 12.1 Daily Operations\n   912→\n   913→```bash\n   914→# Check service health\n   915→docker ps --format "table {{.Names}}\\t{{.Status}}\\t{{.Ports}}"\n   916→\n   917→# View logs\n   918→docker logs --tail 100 matomo-app\n   919→docker logs --tail 100 -f mailserver\n   920→\n   921→# Check disk usage\n   922→df -h /mnt/*\n   923→docker system df\n   924→```\n   925→\n   926→### 12.2 Weekly Operations\n   927→\n   928→```bash\n   929→# Update containers\n   930→docker compose pull\n   931→docker compose up -d\n   932→\n   933→# Clean old images\n   934→docker image prune -a --filter "until=168h"\n   935→\n   936→# Verify backups\n   937→ls -la /backup/\n   938→```\n   939→\n   940→### 12.3 Monthly Operations\n   941→\n   942→```bash\n   943→# OS updates\n   944→sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y\n   945→\n   946→# SSL certificate check\n   947→sudo certbot certificates\n   948→\n   949→# Review firewall rules\n   950→sudo ufw status verbose\n   951→\n   952→# Audit Docker networks\n   953→docker network ls\n   954→docker network inspect public_net\n   955→```\n   956→\n   957→### 12.4 Dashboard Usage\n   958→\n   959→The unified `cloud-dashboard.py` provides three modes: TUI, API Server, and CLI.\n   960→\n   961→```bash\n   962→# Launch interactive TUI dashboard\n   963→python cloud-dashboard.py\n   964→\n   965→# Start Flask API server (for web dashboard)\n   966→python cloud-dashboard.py serve\n   967→python cloud-dashboard.py serve --debug\n   968→\n   969→# Quick CLI status check\n   970→python cloud-dashboard.py status\n   971→\n   972→# Help\n   973→python cloud-dashboard.py help\n   974→```\n   975→\n   976→#### API Endpoints (when running `serve`)\n   977→\n   978→| Endpoint | Description |\n   979→|----------|-------------|\n   980→| `GET /api/health` | API health check |\n   981→| `GET /api/vms` | List all VMs |\n   982→| `GET /api/vms/<id>` | Get VM details |\n   983→| `GET /api/vms/<id>/status` | VM health status (ping, SSH) |\n   984→| `GET /api/vms/<id>/containers` | Docker containers on VM |\n   985→| `GET /api/services` | List all services |\n   986→| `GET /api/services/<id>` | Get service details |\n   987→| `GET /api/services/<id>/status` | Service health status (HTTP check) |\n   988→| `GET /api/dashboard/summary` | Full dashboard with health checks |\n   989→| `GET /api/dashboard/quick-status` | Quick status (config only, no checks) |\n   990→| `GET /api/config` | Full JSON configuration |\n   991→| `POST /api/config/reload` | Reload configuration from disk |\n   992→\n   993→#### TUI Commands\n   994→\n   995→| Key | Action |\n   996→|-----|--------|\n   997→| `1` | VM Details |\n   998→| `2` | Container Status |\n   999→| `3` | Reboot VM |\n  1000→| `4` | Restart Container |\n  1001→| `5` | View Logs |\n  1002→| `6` | Stop/Start Container |\n  1003→| `7` | SSH to VM |\n  1004→| `8` | Open URL |\n  1005→| `S` | Quick Status |\n  1006→| `R` | Refresh |\n  1007→| `Q` | Quit |\n  1008→\n  1009→### 12.5 Incident Response\n  1010→\n  1011→**If container compromised**:\n  1012→```bash\n  1013→# 1. Isolate container\n  1014→docker network disconnect public_net compromised-container\n  1015→docker stop compromised-container\n  1016→\n  1017→# 2. Preserve evidence\n  1018→docker commit compromised-container evidence:$(date +%s)\n  1019→docker logs compromised-container > /tmp/incident-logs.txt\n  1020→\n  1021→# 3. Restore from backup\n  1022→docker compose down compromised-service\n  1023→rm -rf /mnt/public/compromised-data/*\n  1024→# Restore from backup...\n  1025→docker compose up -d compromised-service\n  1026→\n  1027→# 4. Post-incident\n  1028→# - Review logs\n  1029→# - Update passwords\n  1030→# - Patch vulnerabilities\n  1031→# - Update monitoring\n  1032→```\n  1033→\n  1034→---\n  1035→\n  1036→## 12A. subprocess.run([\'ccusage\', ...])\n  1250→                    │\n  1251→                    └── /api/costs/ai/* endpoints\n  1252→```\n  1253→\n  1254→**ccusage Commands (all support --json):**\n  1255→```bash\n  1256→ccusage blocks -a --json      # Current 5h block with projections, burn rate\n  1257→ccusage daily --json -b       # Daily breakdown with model costs\n  1258→ccusage monthly --json -b     # Monthly totals with model breakdown\n  1259→ccusage weekly --json -b      # Weekly aggregation\n  1260→ccusage session --json        # Per-conversation breakdown\n  1261→ccusage blocks --live         # Real-time TUI monitoring\n  1262→```\n  1263→\n  1264→**API Endpoints (direct ccusage integration):**\n  1265→```\n  1266→GET /api/costs/ai/now      → ccusage blocks -a --json\n  1267→GET /api/costs/ai/daily    → ccusage daily --json -b\n  1268→GET /api/costs/ai/monthly  → ccusage monthly --json -b\n  1269→GET /api/costs/ai/weekly   → ccusage weekly --json -b\n  1270→```\n  1271→\n  1272→**Flask Implementation (simple subprocess):**\n  1273→```python\n  1274→import subprocess, json\n  1275→\n  1276→@app.route(\'/api/costs/ai/now\')\n  1277→def api_costs_ai_now():\n  1278→    result = subprocess.run([\'ccusage\', \'blocks\', \'-a\', \'--json\'],\n  1279→                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)\n  1280→    return jsonify(json.loads(result.stdout))\n  1281→\n  1282→@app.route(\'/api/costs/ai/daily\')\n  1283→def api_costs_ai_daily():\n  1284→    result = subprocess.run([\'ccusage\', \'daily\', \'--json\', \'-b\'],\n  1285→                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)\n  1286→    return jsonify(json.loads(result.stdout))\n  1287→```\n  1288→\n  1289→**UI Components:**\n  1290→- Current 5h window: Usage bar, token breakdown, burn rate\n  1291→- Budget tracker: MTD vs limit, projected EOM cost\n  1292→- Model distribution: Pie chart (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus %)\n  1293→- Daily trend: Sparkline of cost over time\n  1294→- Alerts: Warning when Opus > 10%, budget > 75%\n  1295→\n  1296→### 12A.6 Dashboard Tab Structure\n  1297→\n  1298→```\n
